effective.basis: Old state: UDE official card rulings (Sangan/Witch: 'If you have no eligible monsters, your opponent gets to see your Deck to verify', captured 2005-06-16) through Konami's own per-set rulings documents - Machina Mayhem (2010-04-06, 18 days before the Edison snapshot), Starstrike Blast (2010-11-16), Storm of Ragnarok (2011-02-02). New state: KDE-US Tournament Policy section 'Card/Hand/Deck Verification' forbids verifying the opponent's Deck (first located capture 2019-04-03; still current in v2.5, 2025-09-05). No dated announcement of the change was found, so the interval 2011-02-02 .. 2019-04-03 stays open.

corroboration.title: UDE official Yu-Gi-Oh! Card Rulings (capture 2005-06-16, inside the GOAT window)
corroboration.quote: You must show your opponent the monster you select from your Deck for this card's effect. If you have no eligible monsters, your opponent gets to see your Deck to verify.

corroboration.title: Konami, Machina Mayhem Structure Deck Card Rulings, compiled April 6th 2010 (18 days before the Edison snapshot)
corroboration.quote: If you do not have "Commander Covington" in your Deck, your opponent can ask to verify.

corroboration.title: Konami, Storm of Ragnarok Card Rulings, compiled February 2 2011 - the latest positive attestation of the old state
corroboration.quote: If there is no longer a monster in your hand that you can Special Summon when this effect resolves, your opponent may briefly verify that this is the case.

changes.historical_text: When this card is sent from the field to the Graveyard, select 1 monster with a DEF of 1500 or less from your Deck, show it to your opponent, and add it to your hand. Then shuffle your Deck.
changes.modern_text: When this card is sent from the field to the Graveyard: Add 1 monster with 1500 or less DEF from your Deck to your hand.
changes.summary: Period procedure, not a text erratum: the mandatory sent-to-Graveyard search is activated regardless (neither script gates activation on a valid target), and when no monster with 1500 or less DEF remains in the Deck the goat script proves the whiff by revealing the Deck (Duel.GoatConfirm(tp,LOCATION_DECK)) - the ONLY behavioural line separating the goat variant from the pre-errata variant, which is otherwise identical. The printed text meanwhile shed only its procedural select/show/shuffle wording (v1 SKE-020 -> v3 BP01-EN001) with no change to what the effect does; the reveal of the added card itself (Duel.ConfirmCards) survives in the modern script.

effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the errata'd text (BLLR-EN046, Battles of Legend: Light's Revenge)

changes.historical_text: When this card is sent from the field to the Graveyard: Add 1 monster with 1500 or less DEF from your Deck to your hand.
changes.modern_text: If this card is sent from the field to the GY: Add 1 monster with 1500 or less DEF from your Deck to your hand, but you cannot activate cards, or the effects of cards, with that name for the rest of this turn. You can only use this effect of "Witch of the Black Forest" once per turn.
changes.summary: Functional erratum: the added monster (and cards with its name) cannot be activated for the rest of the turn, and the effect becomes a hard once per turn. Both historical scripts show the pre-erratum state - neither the goat nor the pre-errata variant registers the modern e1:SetCountLimit(1,id) nor the EFFECT_CANNOT_ACTIVATE name-lock block with s.aclimit - so before this printing the search had no name-lock and could resolve more than once per turn.

review.notes: Chain starts at lineage v1 (SKE-020), the version the goat baseline implements; v0 (MRD-116, 2002) precedes it and is behaviourally identical. v2 (MRD-116 in Legendary Collection, 2010-10-01) is a cosmetic intermediate between v1 and v3 and is folded into the first change. Unlike the other searchers in this batch, the goat variant relaxes NO activation condition - Witch's trigger is mandatory and neither script tests for a valid target - so only the verification half of the era package applies here and both changes are datable; no chronology-unresolved flag. The shared verification chronology's own evidence includes the 2005-06-16 UDE ruling written for this card, and EdisonFormat.com's period reference corroborates the behaviour independently.
